findings.source: UG1085 v2.5 p113, local text lines6027-6038
findings.assessment: External APB RAM access requires PMU sleep; active CPU accesses can starve external access and hang the system.
IPI0 handler disables interrupts and sleeps before loading/wake sequence. This assumes handler execution and does not establish recovery from a stuck load.
MB_SLEEP field candidate outside PMU RAM. Header defines encoding, not full read side effects, state synchronisation, access permissions or stable residency.
POR clears PMU state; SRST preserves much local/global and PS power state. No tested independent host-controlled recovery from arbitrary hung local transaction is established.

retrieval.result: web open inaccessible; search did not return exact UG1087 entry; Versal PMC results excluded

required_before_hw: Exact UG1087 PMU_GLOBAL register semantics, nonclearing/read safety and master-access scope.
Same-image/session terminal lifecycle plus no-wake/exception argument across status check and RAM read (TOCTOU remains).
Independent recovery path with justified effect on stuck transaction, ownership and normal-runtime restoration; cooperative IPI and host process timeout insufficient.
next_safe_step: Offline obtain exact UG1087 register definition and inspect existing read-only observer transports for semantics and race model. No hardware reads or new executor.
